text:
mia (Docs): hey team, i'm putting together a short docs PR for audit log handling: storage locations, retention defaults, redaction capabilities, and a tiny SDK example for setting policies. can security/legal weigh in on the exact wording?
liam (Security): quick note: default retention is 90 days for hosted. Dedicated/Private customers can set longer/shorter via contract. also we should call out that exports to external sinks may have independent retention.
caroline (Legal): avoid definitive "we delete" language. suggested blurb: "Audit logs are retained for operational and compliance purposes for a configurable period. Customers subject to a contract can request alternative retention terms; legal holds may supersede retention."
mia (Docs): thanks caroline/liam. i'm thinking of a short "what we do" bullet and an "exceptions & limits" bullet. does the legal phrasing above look ok?
caroline (Legal): yes, but add: "We may be required to retain copies to comply with legal obligations." also add a line that redaction is best-effort and may not remove data from previously exported copies.
andre (SDK): i'll add a small Python snippet for the public SDK showing how to create an audit policy. draft:
```py
# create an audit policy via the SDK
policy = client.audit.create_policy(
    key='auth-events',
    retention_days=90,
    redaction_level='pii_partial'  # options: none | pii_partial | pii_full
)
print(policy['policy_id'], policy['effective_retention_days'])
```
andre (SDK): internal note: server expects retention_ttl_days but our SDK maps retention_days -> retention_ttl_days before sending. i'll add a comment in the snippet.
tom (Eng): confirmed. backend field is retention_ttl_days. also, operational caveat: we can't guarantee retroactive redaction for records already exported to external analytic sinks without a migration job. we'll need a migration runbook link in docs.
mia (Docs): adding a short migration checklist for customers + ops. rough steps i'll include: 1) identify exported objects 2) run dry-run re-redaction 3) reconcile diffs 4) apply redaction in batches 5) validate downstream sinks. tom, can you link the runbook once you open the PR?
tom (Eng): yep i'll open a migration PR. will include playbook and rollback steps.
liam (Security): also add a short section about redaction guarantees: "Redaction is best-effort. Customers should assume that copies already forwarded to third-party services may not be affected by redaction commands."
caroline (Legal): tiny edit to the main blurb: change "Customers can request" -> "Customers may request changes in accordance with their contract".
mia (Docs): updated in draft. adding export TTL paragraph and a short FAQ entry: "if my logs were exported, how long before they're gone?" with recommended best-practices.
pr-bot: PR opened by @mia: https://redwood.internal/pulls/5302 - docs/audit-log-retention-redaction-sdk-snippets
andre (SDK): i'll follow up with a small SDK patch to ensure tests cover mapping and a unit test for the sample response. sample response i'll use: {"policy_id": "plc_xyz987", "effective_retention_days": 90} (will include as code block).
tom (Eng): +1 on tests. also add an ops note: schedule migration windows during low traffic and notify customers who requested exports.
liam (Security): please include a short section listing downstream sinks (bigquery, snowflake, splunk) and that customers must manage retention in those systems independently.
mia (Docs): done. i'm going to wait for andre's SDK patch and caroline's signoff. plan: merge docs 24-48h after SDK release to avoid snippet drift. i'll ping #announcements when live.
caroline (Legal): i'll leave comments in the PR now. one more wording nit: prefer "may" over "can" in policy sentences.
mia (Docs): noted & updated. thanks all.
pr-bot: @mia requested reviewers: @andre, @liam, @caroline.
mia (Docs): closing the thread for now; will re-open if reviewers request changes. :memo:
